That's the reassuring one. Downloading the complete backup and getting "Complete library backup downloaded" tells me the whole thing came out in one piece — not just the links and titles, but the parts the browser file couldn't hold: my descriptions, labels, original dates, my written notes with their formatting, and even which ones I'd flagged for later or tucked into the Archive. That's exactly what a backup should be for me — a genuine safety net so that if anything ever went wrong, I could get my entire library back just as it was, not a stripped-down version.

I'll admit that kind of file isn't something I'd open and read myself, so I'm taking it on trust that it truly holds everything you've listed — but that's fine; the point is that it's *complete*, and having both files makes sense to me now: the browser one for moving somewhere else, this one for keeping myself safe.

So getting my collection in and out is settled — import, the browser export, and the full backup all do what I hoped. Good work on this whole transfer piece.
